result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): A fits everything on one week-by-day grid. It brings the earlier units back on Saturdays and in mixed recall, keeps answering from memory central, and uses placeholders for exam details it doesn't know. B also stays within the time limits and teaches the new units first, but its phase templates are harder to read at a glance on a fridge. It also relies more on rereading and skimming, and it assumes 60- and 90-question tests without flagging that as a guess. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): B is the better fridge schedule for this request. It builds the plan around answering from memory, using blank-paper recall, an error log and new practice questions instead of rereading. It uses placeholders instead of guessing exam length or passing score, and puts everything in one week-by-day grid. B's mistakes are that it adds a partial 'Start' week and its dates don't agree: it assumes the exam is on Thursday 17 Dec, but the grid places it on Saturday. A is clear and keeps calculations and drug classes coming back every week, but it relies more on 'review notes' and 'skim'. A also hints at an exam length with its 60- and 90-question tests, and its 90-question test plus review could run past the 90-minute Saturday limit.
